### Scaling modes

- **8h** — P0 rows only; no stretch; business floor 2.5h held; the calendar EXTENDS — the same P0 set takes ~18 months. Hours change depth and calendar, never the P0 deliverable set.
- **15h** — Baseline. Every week row in weeks[] is written at this budget.
- **25h** — Stretch required; a second failure exercise per week; Track F pulls forward; phase 1 compresses to ~8 weeks.

**In-flight recovery.** Never double up after a missed week — slip the calendar. Each week's `recovery` field names the subset to run in the 8h mode. CLARIFIED AT G5b (G5b-01): the enumerated items must FIT WITHIN 8h, not sum to exactly 8.0. W04's happens to reconcile to 8.0; W05's sums to 7.25 and is correct — a subset that fits with room to spare is a better recovery plan than one filled to the ceiling, because a compressed week is compressed precisely when estimates are already under pressure. Prose renders the subset as canon lists it and asserts no total. Sends in particular are never doubled up: the funnel has lead time that hours cannot compress.

## Anti-goals

| Id | Anti-goal | Conditional | Positive form |
|---|---|---|---|
| AG-01 | a generic roadmap | no | Every week names a runnable demo command and a measured number. A week that could be pasted into another person's plan unchanged has failed. |
| AG-02 | a giant list of technologies | no | 30 technologies, each with one of four verdicts and a sequencing note. tracks/*.md open ARTIFACT-FIRST — what the hours buy — and only then list… |
| AG-03 | vague "learn X" recommendations | no | Every P0 concept carries a mastery_check_ref pointing at a deliverable id. A concept with no exercise and no ADR is a P2 or P3 with a stated reason. |
| AG-04 | 50 books | no | 15 resources, three of them books, each with what to learn, which sections, which project and which exercise proves it — plus an explicit exclusion… |
| AG-05 | tutorial projects like basic chatbots | no | Three production-like projects with real integrations: a real GitHub repository, a real Notion workspace, and real historical Sentry issues from the… |
| AG-06 | motivational filler | no | Word CEILINGS as well as floors on every schema. A paragraph that would survive being deleted should be deleted. |
| AG-07 | arbitrary certifications | no | Evidence is a runnable artifact or a measured number. No certification appears anywhere in the portfolio or the competency matrix. |
| AG-08 | LeetCode unless you can justify it for the objective | yes | Answered in low_roi[] LR-07 with the funnel reasoning, and left open as a conditional should the month-12 decision turn toward a role with an… |
| AG-09 | Kubernetes merely because it is "industry standard" | yes | Answered in low_roi[] LR-05: zero surface on one node with one Postgres and git worktrees; roughly two weeks to learn later with a real surface if a… |
| AG-10 | ML theory unrelated to building production AI systems | no | Answered in low_roi[] LR-03. The rigorous quantitative content in this programme is EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN — frozen eval sets, chance-corrected… |
| AG-11 | "build a todo app with AI" | no | The flagship consumes real tasks and real incidents and produces reviewed pull requests against a real repository. Every stage has a runnable demo… |
| AG-12 | passive learning without deliverables | no | Theory is capped at 3.5h per week and 19.4% overall against a 25–30% ceiling; active work is 80.6% against a 70% floor. Every week's deliverables… |

**Conditional handling.** check-antigoals MUST NOT hard-ban the strings 'LeetCode' or 'Kubernetes'. Both anti-goals are CONDITIONAL bans on a REASON, not on a word.
check-antigoals flags an occurrence of either token only when it appears without an adjacent justification or deferral statement within the same section. The two low_roi[] rows are registered as permitted occurrences.
